method_reference: Ramakrishnaiah, C. R., Sadashivaiah, C., & Ranganna, G. (2009). Assessment of Water Quality Index for the Groundwater in Tumkur Taluk, Karnataka State, India. Journal of Chemistry, 6(2), 523-530. https://doi.org/10.1155/2009/757424
standard_source: Bureau of Indian Standards. IS 10500:2012, Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision), Table 2, acceptable limits. https://www.bis.gov.in/
classification_source: Ramakrishnaiah et al. (2009), cited above; weighted-arithmetic WQI classes: 0-25 Excellent, >25-50 Good, >50-75 Poor, >75-100 Very Poor, >100 Unsuitable for Drinking.

excluded_parameters.alkalinity_mg_l: Excluded because the source does not specify the reporting basis (for example, as CaCO3), and its method/standard comparability cannot be verified.

interpretation_note: An aggregate WQI classification is an index result, not a potability certification or a substitute for individual-parameter compliance assessment.
